label: Fictional sample data

eligibility.label: Specific Learning Disability (basic reading skills, reading fluency)

evaluationSummary: Evaluation 2025-10 (fictional results): WISC-V Full Scale IQ 101. WIAT-4 Basic Reading 74, Reading Fluency 72, Reading Comprehension 85, Math Problem Solving 98, Numerical Operations 96. CTOPP-2 Phonological Awareness 78. GFTA-3 standard score 77.
strengths: Grumpy has age-appropriate math reasoning, a strong oral vocabulary, and builds detailed models; he explains his thinking clearly out loud.
needs: Decoding multisyllable and vowel-team words; reading fluency; spelling; producing /r/ and /s/-blends in conversation.
parentConcerns: His family wants him reading chapter books independently and to feel confident reading aloud.
disabilityImpact: Weak phonological processing and decoding limit Grumpy's access to grade-level text in every subject. Articulation errors affect intelligibility to unfamiliar listeners.

presentLevels.text: Reads 48 words correct per minute on grade 2 passages (fictional DIBELS-style probe, Aug 2026; grade 3 fall benchmark about 70). Decodes CVC words 90%, CVCe and vowel-team words 55%. Listening comprehension is at grade level.
Spells closed-syllable and silent-e words 40% correctly in dictation; ideas are strong when he dictates.
Grade-level computation and reasoning; needs word problems read aloud.
Produces /r/ correctly in 30% of words and /s/-blends in 50% of words; intelligible to familiar listeners.

specialFactors.notes: Text-to-speech and audiobooks for content-area reading.

transition.note: Not required: the student is in elementary school (Georgia requires a transition plan by 9th grade entry or age 16).
